H.title: The required D7 export confinement is absent
H.scenario: The M7 callback invokes _build_and_publish through asyncio.to_thread in the server process. There is no separate worker process/unit, worker entry point, runtime cap, LimitFSIZE, read-only snapshot bind, restricted output directory or kernel network denial. The module digest is recorded but no launched worker identity is verified. Cancellation cannot terminate this thread; export work can continue while export() removes its snapshots. A large or blocked export can occupy the host executor indefinitely and has server filesystem/network authority. The stdlib-only comment says the module can run confined, which does not supply confinement.
H.fix: Implement the separate digest-pinned export worker and supervisor with the D7 limits and effective-control validation, reusing the actual A4 service-property/lifecycle seams with export-specific identity and mounts. Add network-denial, output-boundary, runtime/FSIZE and cancellation/crash tests. D7 states this in B4 execute and section 7 relies on it; no accepted named deferral was found. Carrying LOCAL_REGULAR_FILE_IO from B2 does not amend D7. Any deferral requires an explicit design/acceptance amendment before route activation.

M.title: Host publication follows an exports symlink outside the project
M.scenario: mkdir(exist_ok=True), Path opens, os.replace and directory fsync all use pathname resolution through project/exports. O_NOFOLLOW on the worker destination protects only its final component. A pre-existing exports symlink to an outside directory is accepted; the live probe successfully published the archive there. The safe open_beneath used for source assets does not protect snapshots or publication. A confined builder alone will not fix this host-side publisher.
M.fix: Pin and validate the project/export directories with descriptor-relative no-follow traversal; use the owned directory descriptor for private snapshot/partial creation, rename and directory fsync. Open and verify published regular files without following links, and reject root/ancestor swaps. Add pre-existing and raced exports-symlink regressions.

M.title: Localization path collisions silently replace metadata
M.scenario: Localized documents are inserted into a dict after lossy lowercase slugging, before the manifest can reject duplicate paths. A checked candidate containing en and EN has no packaging-rule failures but exports just one metadata/en.json. Locale metadata also overwrites the mandatory metadata/metadata.json, dropping its audience/disclosure fields. The resulting archive and manifest agree on the silently reduced set, so digest verification does not catch the loss.
M.fix: Reserve the primary metadata path and validate every normalized, case-folded destination before inserting any entry. Reject collisions rather than overwriting. Add valid-candidate service/materialization RED cases for en/EN, slug collisions and the reserved metadata locale, asserting no invocation/receipt.

M.title: Disk-full and publication errors leave partial archives
M.scenario: Only ExportBuildError triggers unlink. OSError from build/write/fsync and errors from os.replace occur outside that cleanup policy. Fault probes left partial files for both ENOSPC after partial creation and EIO at rename. M7 then records FAILED_BEFORE_ACCEPTANCE via its generic Exception handler, but export() removes only snapshots; repeated failed commands accumulate potentially multi-GB partials. This violates D7 known-failure cleanup.
M.fix: Own the partial in a try/finally spanning build, rename and verification, removing it on every ordinary failure and cancellation once worker termination is established. Map known disk/rename failures to the typed export failure while preserving unexpected/ambiguous outcome classification. Retain content-addressed objects where outcome recovery requires them. Persist ENOSPC, fsync, rename and cleanup-error regressions.

M.title: The orphan sweep deletes active export work
M.scenario: sweep_partials deletes every matching partial and snapshot without an attempt lookup, ownership/lease check or exclusion of active materialization. A probe with .snapshot-active/member and .partial-active.zip removed both. Running the documented sweep while another command is snapshotting/building can destroy its inputs or unlink its live output. D7 permits sweeping terminal/unknown attempts, not all attempts; snapshot names do not even encode an execution id.
M.fix: Associate scratch ownership with an invocation/execution and safely determine terminal or SUBMIT_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN eligibility, accounting for pre-PLANNED materialization and workers that may still be running. Alternatively enforce a provable exclusive offline sweep boundary. Add concurrent active/sweep and eligible-orphan tests; do not infer orphanhood solely from a filename.

M.title: The complete ZIP operational envelope is not admitted before PLANNED
M.scenario: The manifest bounds entry payloads, excluding manifest bytes and ZIP headers/central directory. A probe materialized exactly 2,147,483,647 payload bytes plus a 1,255-byte manifest; only build_archive refused it, after invocation/PLANNED in the real service. The refusal is ExportIntegrityFailedError instead of M10_OPERATIONAL_ENVELOPE_EXCEEDED. Separately, stdlib zipfile.open reserves a 5 percent size margin: a 2,100,000,000-byte member, below the documented cap, already raises LargeZipFile with allowZip64=False. The source-only module digest also does not identify a Python runtime change affecting ZIP behavior.
M.fix: Preflight selected members plus canonical manifest and exact archive overhead, the writer count/offset limits and zipfile size-margin behavior before copying large inputs and before PLANNED. Raise OperationalEnvelopeExceededError for envelope refusal. Adjust the writer or explicitly amend the supported limit, and pin/qualify the runtime as needed for deterministic bytes. Add allocation-free boundary tests asserting no invocation/attempt on rejection.

M.title: No production asset path reaches the required captions locale layout
M.scenario: member_path has a locale parameter but materialize and _media_of never pass it; PackagingAsset supplies no locale field. A captions SRT asset therefore becomes assets/captions.srt (or assets/captions-en.srt for variant en), never the D6 captions/<locale>.srt path. The worker golden vector manually supplies captions/en.srt and therefore does not exercise this missing service mapping.
M.fix: Define an unambiguous authoritative caption-locale mapping using the existing domain contract if available, or an explicit reviewed contract amendment. Apply it consistently in materialization and media lookup. Add an end-to-end selected-caption export test that inspects both ZIP names and manifest entries, including multiple locales.

M.status: CONFIRMED source validation gap; corruption scenario not exercised on PG
M.title: Recovery does not bind the accepted archive back to the persisted execution manifest
M.scenario: Finalize checks only that the published blob hashes to the digest in provider_job_id. It does not read manifest.json or verify its bytes/member set against invocation.manifest. The invocation reader validates a manifest against its own stored digest but ignores stored request_json, does not recompute identity_digest and does not compare that identity/task/request with the M7 attempt. Thus a cross-bound or corrupt ACCEPTED record pointing at a different self-consistent blob can be receipted alongside this invocation’s manifest; even a non-ZIP blob with its matching accepted digest passes the file check. This is a missing D7 independent recovery invariant, not a claim that SHA256 can be bypassed or that ordinary untampered builds produce wrong bytes.
M.fix: Reconstruct and verify the full stored request/execution identity and its selection/manifest bindings on read; validate attempt task/route/request identity against it. Verify the accepted archive’s exact canonical manifest and member closure before SUCCEEDED/receipt. Do bulk archive verification outside locks against a pinned object, then revalidate authoritative identities and currentness in the final transaction. Add cross-bound attempt, altered identity, wrong embedded manifest, extra/missing member and non-ZIP recovery refusals.

L.status: CONFIRMED; service manifest validation narrows exposure
L.title: The standalone worker accepts paths outside the frozen archive contract
L.scenario: The builder rejects absolute paths, non-ASCII, trailing slash and literal .. segments, but accepts uppercase/case-colliding names, doubled separators, dot segments, backslash, colon and NUL. The probe accepted A.txt with a.txt; a NUL filename was truncated by ZipInfo. Current service-generated ExportManifest paths are stricter, so this is a worker-boundary gap rather than a demonstrated export-service path escape. It matters when this module becomes the D7 separate worker.
L.fix: Validate the complete lowercase normalized path grammar, reserved manifest path and case-folded uniqueness at the worker boundary before opening the destination. Persist the missing RED vectors and reject NUL explicitly.
